user_input: What is a Large Language Model (LLM) in the context of electronic design automation?
reference: An LLM is an advanced artificial intelligence system trained on vast amounts of text data that can understand and generate human-like text. In electronic design automation, LLMs are used to write hardware description languages (like Verilog), generate testbenches, and assist engineers with schematic designs and debugging.

user_input: What is the main advantage of the VAE → RL hybrid strategy over using just pure RL for design-space exploration?
reference: The VAE → RL strategy uses a Variational Autoencoder to compress design parameters into a compact latent manifold. This allows the Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent to explore this space much faster and makes policy learning more stable by removing noise from the inputs, reducing exploration time compared to operating in the raw design space.
reference_contexts: For vast design spaces, VAE→RL compresses a lot of design parameters into a smooth latent manifold that an RL agent can explore quickly. This frequently cuts down on exploration time and makes policy learning more stable by removing noise from inputs.
